en: That Givel... to have come this\nfar in such a short time...!

Mastima. Reports regarding the
damage in each sector are
coming in. I will share them with
you.
Yeah.
Tika, Ricardo.
Right! I'll go arrange the rescue\nteam immediately!
And what about you, big\nbrother...?
I'll just go see if there are any\nother intruders lurking around.
Okay! Please do!
I'm counting on you, you two.
You got it! Rekoro, let's go!
Understood!

This is Tika Blanche. Please
deploy medical teams from
Grand Meteora! I will take
command on-site!
...Tika really has grown strong,\nhasn't she?
Yeah. To be honest, I don't\nknow if I could face her\nhead-on right now.
It simply shows how strong her\nwill was.
It seems she's even gained\nsocial standing within Ex Giva...
She's a strong girl.
For Tika's sake, we seriously\nneed to stay sharp from here\non out!
Hey, you lot. Verda Kleiman,\nand Valka S90.
Hmm?
...What is it?
All three of you, a word.
What on earth is going on?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> After the battle you\njust fought, I wish to ask you\nonce more: are you prepared?
<font color=blue>Verda</font> Prepared?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Are you willing to\nsacrifice your own lives for the\nsake of total strangers?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> I do not understand the\nintent of your question, Master\nMastima.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> The battles ahead in
Daftine will be far more
dangerous than you can
imagine.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> So what of it?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> The three of you are\nnot from this star system.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> asks if you have the
resolve to fight a life-or-death
battle for the future of this
star system.

<font color=blue>Verda</font> That's right, that's right.
Isn't that why you had us
modify our ship? You're a bit
late for this, aren't you?

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> When you first arrived
in this sector, you failed to
realize that Ex Giva was
located on this satellite.
However, on the other hand,\nwhile Givel knew that Ex Giva\nwas here,
They bypassed my Crest\nBarrier and sent such a\nmonster after us.
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Do you understand\nthe meaning of this?
<font color=blue>Valka</font> T-That is...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> I do not know if Ex\nanticipated this,

but the enemy you are about
to face is more dangerous the
more you rely on the common
sense of advanced planets.
Especially for those who try to\napply "common sense" to this\nuniverse.

<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Whether they use
Summoning Crest Arts or serve
Daftes, trivial assumptions can
lead to irreversible
catastrophe.

What you are about to
encounter is "the unknown"
itself, something that cannot
even be compared to me.

Being protected by the
technology of advanced
planets offers no guarantee of
safety.
<font color=blue>Verda</font> What about you?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> Me?
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> How long do you think\nI have resided in this star\nsystem?

I hate to say it, but the level of
attachment Tika and the
others have is different from
mine.

Especially you, Valka S90. Your
assigned mission is
investigation, not intervention
in local affairs.

If you were to fall here, there
would be no one left to return
to Ex with information
regarding Givel or Daftine.

That would result in a
significant loss to the universe,
which is protected by the
power of Vandione and Ex.
That is not what I desire.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...
<font color=blue>Mastima</font> If you are concerned\nabout your comrade Evelysse,
I could likely help you spirit\nthem away from Givel's grasp,\nso if you wait here...
Mastima. You're surprisingly\nkind, aren't you?
But I don't want you to\nmisunderstand. The Captain,\nValka, and of course, I myself,
Are you referring to the\noutcome regarding that burning\ndeath disease?
If you know, then we can skip\nthe formalities.

The Captain, Eve, and Coro
too―they all risked their lives
to face the Levarance
calamity, despite having
nothing to gain from it.
Their resolve is beyond doubt.\nAnd mine is no different.
Besides, as for me, it is even\nsimpler, Mastima.
I am only 13 years old this\nyear. I am still just a child!
What of it?
A child knows all too well that\nthe world is full of things\nunknown.
I will not let my guard down.
For carelessness is the\ngreatest cause of overlooking\nnew things.
...No matter what Tika says,\nshe will surely mention the\nname Verda Kleiman first.
Compared to a mere adult,\nyour wit and composure are on\nan entirely different level.
I am honored by your praise.
And I give you my word.

The Captain, Valka, Eve, and of
course myself―none of us have
the option to walk away from
this fight.

Mastima said it himself, didn't
he? Givel's actions threaten
not just the Twin Stars, but
the entire universe.

Therefore, we will not allow
ourselves to be sidelined from
this battle just because we
aren't from the Twin Stars.
For Tika, for Euwin and the\nothers, and of course for\nMastima, we shall fight!
Verda says all this, but should\nwe double-check just in case?
I see. ...How about you?
But I have learned from the\ngreatest warrior... from my\nfather's way of life...
That the core of that mission\nis to protect the peaceful lives\nof every living being.
Fighting Givel here, right now,\nis something I must do for\nmyself as well.
...I see.
Did you finally convince him?
My apologies. I asked a\ntactless question.
Once Tika and the others\nreturn, I want to brief them on\nthe upcoming plan.
And also...
No, it's nothing.
I'm going to check on Tika and\nRicardo. You all stay here and\nwait.
I suppose when you've lived as\nlong as she has, things get a\nbit complicated.
...Verda, you're really not\nchildish at all. Are you actually\nmuch older than you look?
Who knows? Maybe it's just\nthat the density of life is\ndifferent?
...That's a tough one.
We don't have a moment to\nlose!

If we don't defeat that Givel
quickly, it could affect not only
Daftine and Daftes, but the
entire universe!
Now! There's no time! Is\neveryone here!? I'm going to\nexplain the plan!
Deploy the screen! Hurry,\nhurry!
Y-yes, sir...!
I mean, Mastima, aren't you\nacting a bit hyper? Did\nsomething good happen?
Never mind that, just hurry up!
Whatever, but for now, that is\nthe Captain's seat.
And Coro, why are you moving\non Mastima's orders instead of\nthe Captain's?
Eh? Ah, well, that's...
...Oh, it's nothing.
Hmm... indeed.

We'll depart once we've
assessed Baschen's Imperial
Castle and fed that data into
Coro.

Now, let's not bicker over
trifles. I am the only one who
understands the specifications
of this modified ship.
For now, yield your seat to me!\nUntil the briefing is finished...
Why don't you just go sit in a\ncorner somewhere?
Why are you flustered now that\nwe've come this far?
I had a feeling, but she is quite\nan elusive person.

That's Mastima's true
personality. It's proof that
lifespan and mental maturity
don't always go hand in hand.

Mastima! You can't do that!
This ship belongs to the
Captain, so listen to what they
say!
Aww, Tika... I don't want to\nlisten to a youngster like that.
You're 3.7 billion years old!\nStop acting like a child!

Come on, Coro too! Listen to
the Captain! Mastima, you
made your own seat, so go
move over there!
And Captain, don't get all\ndepressed just because\nMastima teased you!
Everyone, let's get moving!!
Y-Yes, ma'am!
Hmph. Tika is so stubborn.
And yet, you're still going to\nlisten to what Tika says.
Even I didn't realize my own\nsister had such a brisk\npersonality until I came here.
I guess when there's an age\ngap, there are things you just\ncan't see.
...An age gap... means things\nare unseen, huh.
Eu-bo? What's wrong?
Huh? Oh, no, it's nothing.
It's nothing...
So, fine, the Captain can take\ncommand, but what's the\nactual outline of the plan?
Hmm. It is not that\ncomplicated.
First, we just need to destroy\nthe Holy Land of Asyl and the\nblack sphere.

Asyl will surface in response to
the new Gem I am about to
activate, so we'll use Coro's
main cannon to...
Boom! Just like that!
Rest assured.

Coro says the GFSS-3214F's
armament is now stronger than
the Galactic Federation's latest
cutting-edge combat vessels.
Asyl will be blown to\nsmithereens in a single shot!
You say "blown to smithereens"\nso easily, but is it really that\nsimple?

I told you, I've researched this
sector's phenomena since
before the Holy Land War. You
can trust me on that.

A long time ago, we had
already reached the stage
where we could destroy Asyl
whenever we wanted.
The reason I chose not to do\nso was partly because I felt it\nwas helping people.
Huh!?

Among those emerging from
the Moonshadow Ladder, some
rare individuals hail from far-off
sectors with no connection to
the Ladder at all.

They are washed up here after
being swallowed by space-time
rifts that have nothing to do
with the Ladder or Asyl.
Once I realized we were able to\nprotect such people, I couldn't\nbring myself to stop it.
You could say we were\nperforming an act of mercy.
Well, I guess there's more than\none way to put it...?

However, it would be a
different story if someone
other than myself were to
misuse them.
I will never tolerate others\nmanipulating what I have\ncreated without my permission.
That very mindset is part of\nwhy the Ladder was born in\nthe first place.
Hmm? Wait, Master Mastima.

If we destroy the Moonshadow
Ladder and Asyl, the Ladder
won't appear in the future,
right?
That is correct.

Then something doesn't add
up. If that's the case, I can't
explain why Lady Tika and
General Ricardo are here.

...Mastima just said it. People
who have nothing to do with
the Ladder are drifting in here
too.
It was something I wasn't\naware of when I rescued Tika,\nbut...

Ricardo's Daftine Space Force
escort ship caught a faint
glimpse of the person who
attacked the transport ship.
What did you say!?

Back in my day, the Daftine
military reported that several
allied advanced planets were
being invaded by a mysterious
force.

At the time, we'd seen an
Empire ruled by an Integrated
Will Lifeform in deep space, so
I assumed they were that kind
of crowd...
But it turns out I was the only\none who realized it wasn't.
Only you, Ricardo?
<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> At the time, I was the\nfire control officer on the\nescort ship.
That's why I saw it.

From an extreme distance
where I didn't even think it
could hit, a Class 3 energy
wave was emitted.
If you saw the source of that,\nyou'd be even more shocked.

It wasn't a spacecraft or a
fixed battery... that movement...
no matter how you look at it, it
was that of an organic lifeform.
<font color=blue>Valka</font> ...That's impossible...!
<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> It was a shot fired\nfrom an inconceivable distance.
No, I don't even know if it was\nactually a shot.

But what appeared in that
low-resolution footage
captured by the fire control
computer was...
<font color=blue>Welch</font> ...W-what was that?

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> ...Anyway, the moment I
saw that footage, my escort
ship took an unexplained hit
and sank.
Well, I suppose we were hit\ndirectly by that Class 3\nenergy.
I don't know how I ended up\ndrifting to the Ex Giva after\nthat, but...

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> Even if a monster
capable of unleashing Class 3
energy was involved, it wouldn't
be all that unnatural.
<font color=blue>Henri</font> So, common sense\ndoesn't apply in space, then.

But if we believe Mastima's
explanation, even if the
periodic Moonshadow Ladder
stops occurring,
The possibility remains that the\ncurrent Ladder could cause a\nrift in future spacetime, right?

We can't rule out the possibility
that we were caught up in it.
We mustn't jump to
conclusions.

<font color=blue>Ricardo</font> Yeah, true. Besides,
there's nothing Tika and I can
do right now to get back to
our own era.
Let's try not to overthink\nthings.

In any case, destroying the
Ladder and Asyl now offers
more benefits than leaving
them as they are.
However, in the end, we must\nstop that fool from Givel.

After destroying Asyl, we'll
likely storm the Baschen
Imperial Castle. From there, it
will be hand-to-hand combat.

We can't afford to turn the
power capable of destroying
Asyl toward the Imperial Castle
or the Imperial Capital...
We can't afford to lose this\ntime.
Mastima, will you be joining us\nin that battle?
I'll have to teach that cocky\nbrat a lesson, after all.
Besides, I bear the\nresponsibility for letting him\nlearn about the Gems here.
Givel learned...? Then...
What's wrong?
Hey, Eu.
Hmm? What is it, Welch?
...Take this!!
Agh!? Wh-wh-what are you\ndoing all of a sudden!!
Eu! Get it together right now!
Huh!?
What is it that you need to be\nthinking about right now!!
What are you even talking\nabout all of a sudden!
Ending the Holy Land War, of\ncourse! Blowing Givel to\nsmithereens, of course!
I-I know that...
Then why are you thinking\nabout Father and Brother right\nnow!!

How many years do you think
we've been together?! Did you
think you could pull a fast one
on me?!
...Haha, you've got me.
To tell you the truth...

You're projecting Tika and
Ricardo's situation onto
yourself, aren't you? You're so
simple, Eu-bo.
I'd rather not be called simple\nby you, Welch!

You're probably thinking, "Even
though they were so cold,
Father and Brother had no
choice given their positions,"
Or, "If I were in Father's\nposition, I might have thought\nthe same way..."
You're thinking all that trivial\nnonsense, aren't you!
Don't put so much emphasis on\nit being trivial... I have things on\nmy mind, you know...
The only thing you and Tika's\ngroup have in common is the\nage gap between the siblings!
What could you possibly be\nworrying about!?

...Tika and Ricardo have always
been close despite the age
gap, supporting each other
through even the harshest
times, right!?
Did your father or brother try\nto support you, or try to\nunderstand you?
I know the truth. Eu-boy, you\nwere trying your best to find\ncommon ground with them.
But they have no intention of\ndoing the same.
It's obvious to anyone\nwatching. It's nothing like Tika\nand Ricardo.
The one person you really need\nto be thinking about in that\nregard... is Sister Eslyn!
...Yeah, you're right.
Don't lose sight of who you\nshould actually be worrying\nabout.

When push comes to shove,
you want to be thinking about
the people who matter, don't
you?
It's not that I'm trying to deny\nthe Rakstar family's love for\none another, but...

In the battles to come, don't
you think there are things
more important to consider
than Father or Brother?
...Yeah, you're right.
So?
Hmm?
Who exactly are you planning\nto think about?
My companions, I guess?
Ow! What was that for?!
Nothing! I was just giving you a\nlittle pep talk!
See ya! I'm going to go see\nCoro first!
...Sigh.
No, seriously, saying that now\nof all times is... really?
Mastima, do you have a\nmoment?
Hmm?
Do you know anything about\nthe power of the Beast Witch?

Yes, I have heard stories from
Tika and Ricardo, and I am
aware of the records kept by
Coro and Rekoro...

Unfortunately, it seems the
Beast Witch's Crest Arts are
something Givel developed
independently from the Crests
I discovered.
I have not finished analyzing\nthem yet.
Therefore, I cannot delete that\nCrest from you.
That is what you wanted to\nask, isn't it?
It's not that I find this power\nabominable...

I can't forgive Givel, but thanks
to this power, the status of the
Fox Spirit people has improved
dramatically.
It's just...
When I think that this might\nhave been hurting Henri's\ncompanions...
Hmm.
I might hesitate to use this\npower when it truly matters.
I see.
Well, I don't see the harm in\nthat.
What?

Whether you win or lose
against Givel, your life
continues as long as you do
not die.
This is by no means the final\nbattle of your life.
Even I still struggle with the\nnature and morality of my own\npower.
Doubt and worry are often\nseen as shackles, but they can\nalso give rise to new strength.
If you like, I could even conduct\nsome research on it after the\nbattle is over.
...May I take you up on that?

I dislike the fact that this is a
Crest Art created by Givel, but
my curiosity regarding this new
type of Crest outweighs that.
...In fact.
Eh?
I could start researching it\nright this instant, you know?

That crest on your chest―is it
your natural one? Or is it the
crest of the "Witch of the
Beast"? Hmm?
Hyah!? W-wait! What are you\ndoing!?
Hmm? If I'm to research the\ncrest, I can't exactly begin\nwithout touching it, can I?

I-if that's how it's going to be,
not right now, thank you!
S-sometime, when I feel like it!
Bye!!
She's gone...
Hehehe, well, that's just how\nshe is. Did I tease her a bit too\nmuch?
It's finally time.
Yeah.
It's been a long journey to get\nhere.
Yeah.
...If we ever run into Mom and\nDad somewhere, they'll surely\nbe surprised.
Yeah.

...They say that tomorrow,
Coro's stuffed animals will rain
down from the sky during
Dagris.
Yeah.
Hey, big brother!
...Ah, sorry. I was lost in\nthought for a moment.
Yeah, I figured as much.
So, what were you thinking\nabout?
...How to find Mom and Dad.
As long as you and I are here,\nit wouldn't be strange if they\nwere still alive.
I've been thinking about what\nto do once the fighting in\nDaftine in this era is over.

It turned out quite differently
from what I had imagined, but
well, we're managing to get by
somehow.

I thought they might show up if
we waited at Mastima's, but
only Mastima could afford to
wait like that.

Besides, if they traveled
through time for the same
reason we did, they might have
been thrown somewhere else
entirely.
I mean, it's like trying to find\none specific grain of sand in a\ndesert...
...Yeah, you're right.

Come to think of it, Mom and
Dad were still in the middle of
a fight with Grandpa and
Grandma.
If we're going to live separate\nlives, we'll still need to find a\nway to stay in touch.
Yeah...!
But, it'll probably be hard if it's\njust us. We don't even have a\nstarship.
...That's the problem... Damn it.
It feels like we're out of\noptions, doesn't it?
Dammit... This is infuriating.
...Are you worried about\nwhether you can get along with\nMastima?
Wha―!?
H-H-Henri!?
You have a look on your face\nlike you're wondering how I\nknew.
H-H-H-How did you know?!
Well, it's written all over your\nface.
Wh-What!! W-Where?!
No, it isn't actually written\nthere.
Which one is it then?!
...You're quite flustered.
I know Master Mastima isn't a\nbad person...
But I still don't know how I\nshould act around him.
He is just far too elusive...
Hmm.
...I have never... heard the\nnames of EnII or Vandione...
...nor any words that denied\nthe very existence of Ex\nbefore.
For you, Valka, it is as if your\ngods were being denied.
Ex is different from the gods.
Ex is... Ex is...
Judging by your attitude, that\nis the only conclusion I can\ndraw.
...Worried?

...Valka, you seem to rely too
heavily on your own identity as
an existence of Ex and as a
Hardier Warrior of Morphus.

Rather than pride, isn't it a
sense of urgency―a fear of
tarnishing those names―that
takes precedence?
T-That's not true!
...At least, I... think...
We know nothing of this Ex or\nEnII.
You are the only one who\nknows.
So, if you'll take it from me,\nValka.

From the perspective of
someone who knows nothing of
Ex, EnII, or any other Hardier
Warrior of Morphus...
You are a truly remarkable\nperson.
Huh...?

You know how terrifying battle
is and do not seek it, yet you
have the resolve and strength
to fight for the sake of your
friends.
If that is not remarkable, then I\ndo not know what is.
I-I don't...! I don't think... battle\nis terrifying...!
...I don't... think... so...
...I thought... I wasn't allowed to\nfeel that way...

No battle in this world is
without fear. Even without
living as long as Mastima, I can
understand that much.
Proving Mastima wrong will be\neasy.

You simply need to face
combat, just as you have done
alongside the Captain and the
others until now.

If you do, eventually you will
find your own way to deal with
Mastima, a fellow being living in
this same universe.
...You think so?
I know so.
...Sometimes you're like a\nfather, Henri. It's... somehow\ncomforting.
Henri?
...If that is how you feel...
Eh?

I'm heading ahead. I intended
to offer you counsel, but it
seems I was the one who was
saved instead.
Huh? What?
It's nothing.
Farewell.
Oh, okay...
Overcoming things is harder\nthan I thought...
Coro, I'm going to run a few\nchecks before we head out.

While I was messing with the
console earlier, I noticed some
programs and applications I've
never seen before.
I don't want to make a mistake\nby performing some strange\noperation when it really counts.
Rest assured, Captain!

It's true that Mastima-san
tinkered with various things
while she was making
modifications,
But she hasn't touched my\noriginal programming at all!
Hmm? The ship's scanners are\noperating on their own.
Hup!
Eh!?

What is this? There's a
program set up to collect data
from normal space as we pass
through during warp.
Doing something like this will\nmake the drive incredibly\nsluggish. Take this!
Hah!
Ack!?
Coro! Someone's gone and\nmessed with the original\nprogramming!

It's defined so that under
certain conditions, Mastima's
authority supersedes the
Captain's!
I'm deleting this right now!
Waaaaah!?
I-I'm so sorry...!

While none are harmful
individually, it's a problem that
functions unknown to the
Captain are operating on their
own.
At this rate, Mastima might\nend up seizing control of the\nship at any moment!
Verda, could you run a check\non me as well...?
Seeing all this being done to\nCoro... it's making me a little\nuneasy.
Hmm, I suppose so. Come over\nhere.
...Hm? What is this?
I-Is there a problem!?

There's a backdoor. It's set up
so that the human vital data
Rekoro observes is being
transmitted somewhere.
What...!?

There are many entries
regarding Tika. They might
have intended to monitor her
even after she left the
Mastima satellite.
But when did this happen!?
I was threatened by Mr.\nRicardo...

I made sure to classify all of
Tika's personal information as
strictly confidential so no one
could look at it carelessly!
...This is truly malicious. I'll have\nto demand answers from\nMastima later.
We must continue the journey\nof "Coro's Ship" even after we\ndefeat Givel.
And there's no sign of the Holy\nLand War ending anytime\nsoon...
The path ahead looks nothing\nbut difficult.
That's right. We made a\npromise to Tika.
We promised Tika that we\nwould deliver them safely to\ntheir homeland... to Daftine.
In that case, we must learn to\nlaugh off and kick aside\nhardships of this level!
How reassuring.

It is so reassuring that I am
starting to think it might be
better if Verda were the
Captain.
Hmm! In that case, shall we set\nthe Captain's role as "pet"?
Nooooo! I won't lose! I won't\nsubmit to your modifications,\nVerda! I'll definitely resist...!
Wait, but now that I think\nabout it, isn't a "pet Captain"\nactually quite wonderful?
Captain, paw! or "Go get me a\nbanana!"―I could see myself\nsaying things like that...
Waaaaahhh!?

Oh! The runaway suppression
device Mastima made for Coro
is working! We should leave it
as it is!
Ugh, and I was hoping for a\nmuch sharper comeback than\nthat...
Only Eve is capable of keeping\nyou in line with nothing but a\nretort.
Indeed. We must go and fetch\nher as soon as possible.

You're right. I haven't been
verbally abused by Eve-san
yet, so I'm not quite feeling like
myself!
I'm not sure about that, but I\nagree that GFSS-3214F is not\nin a normal state without Eve.
True. It is about time.
It matters not what Mastima is\nthinking, or what despicable\nmethods Givel may employ.
Together with our allies, we\nshall surely bring Eve back and\nfulfill our promise to Tika!
Let's goooo! I'm not staying\nbehind this time either!!
Everyone is here.

Coro and Rapture Day Control
will handle the launch, but once
we're underway, I'm leaving
everything to you.

Right! This ship only truly flies
when the Captain is in that
seat! Oh, I'm just so happy, I'm
so happy!
Coro! Keep your eyes forward\nwhile piloting! Pull yourself\ntogether!
Oh, that's right, that's right!
I won't let my guard down for a\nsingle second from here on\nout!

Upon launch, the Ex Giva will
emit a space-time regression
Gem toward the waters off
Rubarika and Baschen.
The moment Asyl surfaces, we\nwill destroy it with the main\ncannon.
Control has given the okay!\nCoro and GFSS-3214F, launch\nsequence, all systems green!
Hey, make sure everyone's\nharnesses are tight! It's going\nto be a bumpy ride!
The new GFSS-3214F,\ndeparting!
Matched with the planned\nroute!
Mastima!

Alright, Coro! Give the signal to
activate the Spacetime
Regression Gem on Ex Giva!
Lure Asyl out!
